original.target_description: Assigned original: Srull and Wyer, Study 1, hostility interpretations after hostility-related priming. Full primary text unavailable within acquisition budget.

replication.target_description: Primary random-effects meta-analysis across 22 eligible labs: mean ratings of five ambiguously hostile behaviors, 80%-hostile versus 20%-hostile sentence primes; 30 sentences, no delay.

n.sample_role: Analytic participants across 22 laboratories; 2,813 in 20%-hostile and 2,797 in 80%-hostile condition.
n.exclusions: Individual exclusions: incomplete sentence-descrambling task or critical ratings, nonstudents, age outside 18–25, missing gender, failure to follow instructions or other experimenter-recorded reasons. Four labs with fewer than 100 participants per condition excluded from primary analyses; 22 labs retained. N counts participants, not the 22 laboratory estimates.
n.location: p.329, Fig.2, Meta-Analytic Average and caption; pp.325/327 exclusions

notes:
Original reference uses a 2004 book-chapter DOI, while the replication identifies the primary study as Srull and Wyer (1979), Experiment 1, DOI 10.1037/0022-3514.37.10.1660. No full original primary text was obtained; no original values were copied from the replication. The candidate original PDF was abstract-only and rejected. Replication title and DOI verified in full publisher-version PDF. The neutral description identifies ambiguous-behavior judgments, which are distinguished from ratings of the vignette protagonist. Locator p.7 corresponds to article p.327 without repository cover, where both outcome analyses begin; the selected behavior effect continues on p.328. Requested replication metric d is not printed for this target test; the printed raw mean difference is retained without conversion. The d = 0.06 on p.332 concerns the separate protagonist outcome and is not used. No p-value for the selected mean difference is printed in the main report; p = .27 on p.328 tests heterogeneity Q(21) = 24.39 and is not the effect test. The sample size is explicitly reported for primary analyses; 7,373 is the recruited total and 6,404 includes labs excluded from primary analyses.
Completion source review (n_r): Fig.2 identifies final mutually exclusive priming-condition participant counts for the primary ambiguous-behavior outcome, across 22 eligible labs. Individual exclusions: incomplete sentence-descrambling task or critical ratings, nonstudents, age outside 18–25, missing gender, failure to follow instructions or other experimenter-recorded reasons. Four labs with fewer than 100 participants per condition excluded from primary analyses; 22 labs retained. N counts participants, not the 22 laboratory estimates.
Completion source review (es_value_r): The target behavior outcome prints a raw mean difference, not d. No conversion performed. The d≈0.06 in Discussion is for Ronald ratings and is not transferable.
Completion source review (reported_success): Authors conclude these procedures are unlikely to yield a practically and routinely detectable assimilative priming effect; their behavior result is described as opposite the predicted direction. Vocabulary failed reflects this narrative.
